# Cape Town Invest — full page index

Independent research on Cape Town and Western Cape property for foreign buyers. Every page below is public and indexable.

Key facts used across the corpus, current at August 2026 and worth re-verifying before transacting:
- Foreigners may own freehold and sectional title property in South Africa. No foreign buyer surcharge applies.
- Transfer duty runs on the SARS scale effective 1 April 2025: nil to R1,210,000, then 3%, 6%, 8%, 11% and 13% on the top band above R13,310,000.
- New stock sold by a VAT-registered developer carries 15% VAT instead of transfer duty, never both.
- Non-residents typically borrow up to about 50% of the purchase price from South African banks.
- Non-resident sellers face a withholding of 7.5% (individuals), 10% (companies) or 15% (trusts) on prices above R2m, credited against the final capital gains liability.
- Capital gains inclusion is 40% for individuals and 80% for trusts and companies; the primary residence exclusion is R2m.
- City of Cape Town rates for 2026/27 grant a rates-free portion of R620,000 on homes valued at R8,000,000 or less, then charge about 0.0064 in the rand per year; above R8,000,000 no rates-free portion applies.
- A sectional title body corporate can restrict short-term letting by 75% special resolution under the STSMA.
- Property ownership does not grant residency. Visa routes are separate.
- Rental yields on this site are modelled and directional, not guaranteed.

Sources cited across the corpus: Lightstone deeds data, FNB and John Loos research, Pam Golding and Seeff market commentary, SARS guidance, City of Cape Town by-laws and tariffs.

## Areas (26)

- [Bantry Bay Property Investment 2026: The Cliff-Block Levy](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/bantry-bay-property-investment/): Bantry Bay is a ribbon of 1960s cliff blocks. Facade repair, waterproofing and lift replacement decide the return, so the levy schedule is the due diligence.
- [Blouberg Property Investment 2026: Wind Is the Variable](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/blouberg-property-investment/): The south-easter that made Blouberg a world kite-surfing destination also sets its rental season, its maintenance costs and which units let in summer.
- [Camps Bay Property Investment 2026: The Nightly-Let Calendar](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/camps-bay-property-investment/): Camps Bay runs on a seasonal calendar: December carries the year, July empties it, and two permissions can delete the nightly-let case entirely. The arithmetic.
- [Claremont Property Investment 2026: 6% Gross, 4.2% Net](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/claremont-property-investment/): Claremont apartments model 6% gross and 4.2% net at R30k-50k per sqm. Cavendish Square retail and the rail interchange make it the southern suburbs income play.
- [Clifton Property Investment 2026: Structure Beats Yield](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/clifton-property-investment/): At a R30 million Clifton ticket the ownership name decides more than the yield: CGT inclusion of 40% or 80%, and section 35A withholding at 7.5% or 15%.
- [Constantia Property Investment 2026: Above the R8m Line](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/constantia-property-investment/): Constantia is where the City's R620,000 rates-free portion stops applying, since it covers homes at R8 million or less. What that does to holding costs.
- [De Waterkant Property Investment Guide 2026, Yields](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/de-waterkant-property-investment/): De Waterkant property investment guide: modelled 7.8% gross yields, heritage pocket between Green Point and City Bowl, ONEONR Blok nearby, short-let demand.
- [Durbanville Property Investment 2026: Family Yields](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/durbanville-property-investment/): Durbanville property investment: modelled 6% gross on family homes, R15k-R28k psqm, wine-route edge, top schools, and Gauteng semigration demand.
- [Franschhoek Property Investment 2026: A Holding-Cost Market](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/franschhoek-property-investment/): Franschhoek sits in Stellenbosch Municipality, an hour from Cape Town, with no commuter market. Holding cost, not yield, is what a buyer here is choosing.
- [Fresnaye Property Investment 2026: Pricing a Thin Market](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/fresnaye-property-investment/): Fresnaye produces about 17 prime sales a year. That thinness changes how you value a house, and freehold changes what the annual cost stack contains.
- [Gardens Property Investment 2026: Pricing the Gradient](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/gardens-property-investment/): Gardens is a street-position market. Kloof Street frontage, the quiet mid-slope and the upper reaches are three products at three prices that let differently.
- [Green Point Property Investment 2026: The Hybrid Letting Year](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/green-point-property-investment/): Green Point is where a summer short-let and a winter lease genuinely combine, because stadium events and V&A business travel fill the months the beaches lose.
- [Hermanus Property Investment 2026: A Different Municipality](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/hermanus-property-investment/): Hermanus is not in Cape Town. Overstrand Municipality rates at 0.005237 in the rand with a R350,000 threshold, and the 120km drive shapes who rents and when.
- [Hout Bay Property Investment 2026: The Valley's Infrastructure](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/hout-bay-property-investment/): Hout Bay is a valley with three ways out and a harbour economy. Access and private utilities decide the investment here more than the sea view does.
- [Kalk Bay Property Investment 2026: False Bay Guide](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/kalk-bay-false-bay-property-investment/): Kalk Bay property investment: False Bay fishing village, modelled 6.5% gross on cottages, R22k-R45k psqm, UK semigration and mixed long-let demand.

- [Newlands Property Investment 2026: The Wettest Suburb](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/newlands-property-investment/): Newlands takes roughly three times Cape Town's rainfall. Damp, drainage and maintenance decide holding costs here, and the same water built the suburb's value.

- [Table View Property Investment 2026: West Coast Yields](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/table-view-property-investment/): Table View property investment: beach apartments, Rietvlei wetland, modelled 5.5% net yields, R18k-R32k psqm, family semigration on the West Coast corridor.
- [Tamboerskloof Property Investment 2026: Slope and Heritage](https://capetown-invest.com/areas/tamboerskloof-property-investment/): Tamboerskloof climbs Lion's Head, so gradient decides parking and daily use, and its Victorian cottages sit under heritage protection at the 60-year threshold.

## Comparisons (15)

- [Atlantic Seaboard vs Winelands: Two Ownership Regimes](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/atlantic-seaboard-vs-winelands-investment/): One is sectional title on a salt coast, governed by statute. The other is freehold in an HOA estate, in fire and borehole country. The regime decides the work.
- [Cape Town vs Dubai 2026: Currency and the Way Out](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-dubai-property-investment/): Dubai is a dollar asset you can leave freely. Cape Town is a rand asset behind exchange control. The rand is why it is cheap and why the income is small.
- [Cape Town vs Durban 2026: When the Municipality Is the Asset](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-durban-property-investment/): A beachfront property is sold on an amenity the municipality maintains. In Durban that has been tested. What it did to the market, and what a buyer should read.
- [Cape Town vs Johannesburg: Who Sets the Price 2026](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-johannesburg-property-investment/): In Johannesburg the rent sets the price. In Cape Town the price sets the rent. One difference explains the yield gap, the vacancy risk and both exits.
- [Cape Town vs Lisbon 2026: Operating an Apartment Compared](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-lisbon-property-investment/): Lisbon apartments average 4.13% gross yield and carry AIMI above EUR 600,000. Sea Point models 9.7% gross. What each is actually like to run as a landlord.
- [Cape Town vs Mauritius 2026: A Market or a Programme](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-mauritius-property-investment/): Mauritius sells non-citizens a state-designed scheme with a residence permit attached. Cape Town sells the open market itself. That gap decides your exit.
- [Cape Town vs Portugal 2026: The Full Ownership Tax Stack](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-portugal-property-investment/): Portugal charges non-residents a flat 7.5% IMT and annual AIMI above EUR 600,000. South Africa charges a sliding duty to 13% and no wealth layer.
- [Cape Town vs Stellenbosch 2026: Depth Against Concentration](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/cape-town-vs-stellenbosch-property/): Cape Town spreads demand across a metro economy. Stellenbosch concentrates it on one university and one small market, which changes both yield and exit risk.
- [Century City vs Durbanville 2026: Apartment or House Costs](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/century-city-vs-durbanville-investment/): This is a product comparison, not a geography one. A levy that funds a building against a house where every maintenance decision and its cost belongs to you.
- [Century City vs Sea Point: Who Owns the Street](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/century-city-vs-sea-point-investment/): One node's environment is a managed product with a levy and an owner. The other's is a public suburb the City maintains. That sets the cost and the risk.
- [Off-Plan vs Resale Cape Town: Which Unknown You Carry](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/off-plan-vs-resale-cape-town-investment/): Off-plan gives you the price today and the building later. Resale gives you both today. Every other difference, including the tax, follows from that.
- [Paarl vs Stellenbosch 2026: One Town Can Still Grow](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/paarl-vs-stellenbosch-property-investment/): Twenty minutes apart and priced differently because one is hemmed in and the other is not. Supply, not demand, explains the gap in yield, entry and exit.
- [Sea Point vs Camps Bay 2026: Two Different Businesses](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/sea-point-vs-camps-bay-investment/): Sea Point models 7.5% net and re-lets in weeks. Camps Bay models 4.4% and earns in a six-week window. One is an investment, the other is a store of value.
- [Somerset West vs Constantia 2026: The R8 Million Line](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/somerset-west-vs-constantia-investment/): Both sit inside the City of Cape Town, so the rate in the rand is identical. The difference is the R620,000 rates-free portion, which stops above R8 million.
- [Western Cape vs Gauteng 2026: The Cost of the Move](https://capetown-invest.com/compare/western-cape-vs-gauteng-property-investment/): Fifteen years of divergence, absorbed in one transaction. What a Gauteng household realises on the sale, and what the Cape purchase costs on arrival.

## Buyer guides (4)

- [Cape Town Property for UK Retirees: 2026 Buyer Guide](https://capetown-invest.com/segments/cape-town-property-for-uk-retirees/): UK retirees buying in Cape Town: GBP/ZAR, R37k/month retirement visa, medical aid, Southern Suburbs vs Seaboard, POA purchase, and tax on exit.
- [German Buyers in Cape Town: Exemption, Not Credit](https://capetown-invest.com/segments/german-buyers-cape-town-property/): The treaty gives South Africa the taxing right on Cape Town rent, and Germany exempts it while still counting it. Plus the ten-year rule that changes the hold.
- [UK Buyers in Cape Town: Residence, Not Passport](https://capetown-invest.com/segments/uk-buyers-cape-town-property/): A British passport changes nothing in South Africa, and UK residence changes everything at home. Why the answer moves when you do, and what to settle first.
- [US Buyers in Cape Town: Citizenship Follows You](https://capetown-invest.com/segments/us-buyers-cape-town-property/): South Africa treats an American buyer like any other foreigner. The United States does not. What a Cape Town property adds to a US filing obligation.

## Developers (7)

- [Amdec Harbour Arch: Living Inside a Building Site](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/amdec-property-investments/): Tower 1 is finished and the precinct is not. What an owner holds while the cranes are still there, and the parking question that decides a resale.
- [Blok Developers: What a Small Scheme Concentrates](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/blok-urban-developers/): A design-led boutique building is the opposite of a master-planned precinct. Fewer units concentrate the levy, the arrears and the resale pool onto you.
- [Devmco Group Projects 2026 — Sibaya, Umhlanga & Cape Town](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/devmco-group/): Devmco Group: Sibaya R6bn invested, Umhlanga Arch delivered. KZN projects vs Cape Town Harbour Arch — foreign buyer rules, no surcharge.
- [Growthpoint at the V&A: The Counterparty You Can Read](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/growthpoint-waterfront/): It is the one Cape Town development counterparty whose accounts are public and audited. That changes what off-plan due diligence can actually establish.
- [Prospekt: Buying a Tax Allowance and an Operator](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/prospekt-property-development/): Two of the three things being sold are not the apartment. A UDZ allowance you may not be able to use, and an operating arrangement that produces the income.
- [Rabie Property Group: What a Master Developer Owes You](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/rabie-property-developers/): Rabie built Century City and still shapes it. That is a covenant on delivery and a conflict on supply, and both matter to a buyer in the same precinct.
- [Val de Vie: The Estate Is the Asset, Not the House](https://capetown-invest.com/developers/val-de-vie-estate/): About R13,540 a month before bond service buys membership of a place. Whether that is expensive depends entirely on whether you are the one living there.

## Market news (5)

- [Cape Town Rates Hike May 2026: SARB 7%, Prime 10.5% Impact](https://capetown-invest.com/news/cape-town-interest-rates-property-2026/): SARB lifted the repo rate 25bp to 7% in May 2026 and prime to 10.5%. First hike since 2023. Impact on Cape Town bond buyers, affordability and stress tests.
- [Cape Town Luxury Sales Hit R11.3bn Record in 2025](https://capetown-invest.com/news/cape-town-luxury-sales-record-2025/): Atlantic Seaboard and City Bowl luxury sales hit R11.3bn in 2025, up 26%. Ross Levin data: 116 deals above R20m and a R157.55m Clifton record sale.
- [Foreign Buyers Drive Atlantic Seaboard Sales in 2025](https://capetown-invest.com/news/foreign-buyers-atlantic-seaboard-2025/): Foreign buyers took 25% of Atlantic Seaboard value in 2025, about R2.8bn. No SA buyer surcharge and 50% LTV rules keep UK, German, and US demand active.
- [V&A Waterfront Granger Bay: R24bn Expansion, 27k Jobs](https://capetown-invest.com/news/va-waterfront-granger-bay-development/): V&A Waterfront plans ~3.8ha Granger Bay reclamation, R24bn mixed-use build, R8.8bn GDP and 27,000 jobs. Shore protection, residential and hotel — approval 2027.
- [Western Cape Property Forecast: 7.4-9.3% Growth in 2026](https://capetown-invest.com/news/western-cape-property-forecast-2026/): Western Cape prices forecast 7.4-9.3% growth in 2026 vs 6% nationally. Prime Cape Town may consolidate at 5-7% as semigration meets tight inventory.
